gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-istok-web: Rounded letterforms with a clearly open side make Istok Web feel friendly and modern. Istok Web would carry a long page without tiring, while Balsamiq Sans adds stencil-cut heading letters of one steady width.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-jost: Balsamiq Sans draws its heading in the constant weight of a stencil-cut channel, with no tight, pinched curves anywhere. Jost sits below with broad gaps at the terminals and a unit-width stroke.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-jura: Chunky, stencil-cut, and full of nerve. Jura follows in a plain sans with wire-like strokes and s curves that open wide, so the heading gets all the attention while Balsamiq Sans holds the line.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-k2d: Balsamiq Sans leads with bold, expressive stencil-cut letters. K2D keeps a tube-like thickness through every bend, with c terminals that hang far from the bowl, so a long stretch of text moves along smoothly.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-kanchenjunga: Stencil-cut channels of constant weight, with no pinched curves, define Balsamiq Sans. Kanchenjunga brings the other strength: sans-serif shapes that never clog at low resolution, drawn with the steady line of a technical drafting pen.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-kantumruy-pro: Loud, stencil-cut, and unpinched. Kantumruy Pro adds hairline-free, swell-free sans-serif letterforms with an e whose eye opens clearly to the right, and that approachable plainness is what lets Balsamiq Sans stay bold.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-kodchasan: Bold and stencil-cut, with curves that never pinch. Kodchasan reads cleanly beneath it, its terminals hang open and nothing thins like a calligraphic pen, so a long passage runs smoothly.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-koho: Balsamiq Sans lays strokes like fine rope into its letter shapes, bold and expressive up top. KoHo stays quiet below, a sans-serif with wide c apertures, and that gap in temperament is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-kosugi: Balsamiq Sans holds the constant weight of a stencil-cut channel, which gives headings real swagger. Kosugi does the quieter job, bending its sans-serif letters like wire with an open-jawed c like a pair of pliers.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-kosugi-maru: Balsamiq Sans keeps a bold, stencil-cut line with no pinched curves anywhere. And Kosugi Maru follows underneath like neon tubing, sans letters of one steady thickness with stroke ends set far apart.
